data.narrative:
Layup Parts is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Zack Eakin that has raised $2M+. The target operates within a sector populated by 9 comparables: 1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

Two standard valuation methods were assessed for applicability. Stage-progression analysis, which would apply a 2.5x multiplier to a $42M base value derived from total raised proxies, was excluded after a sanity check revealed the resulting $105M valuation would exceed 20x the company's actual $2M fundraising to date—indicating the base value was likely a funding-tracker parsing error. Peer-median triangulation was also deemed inapplicable; while 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, the narrow filter set (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier) yielded only 1 datapoint. Expanding to all-sector medians would introduce undue noise given stage and business model heterogeneity.

The analysis cannot produce a supported valuation range without either reliable stage-adjusted comparable data or cleaner cap table fundamentals. The key uncertainty is the availability of tight peer valuations at the seed stage in this sector. Further diligence should target recent seed-round pricing for Walden Robotics, Divergent, or similar peers, or establish valuation anchors through investor SAFE terms.
